Reported to the mastermind. All five deliverables are built, tested, and committed in the worktree. Summary:

**Spike (`Servex/ext/openrouter/spike.mjs`)** ran for real on three OpenRouter models, key read only from its file, never logged:

| model | tools | stream | edit | resume ok | $real |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| openai/gpt-6-luna | 5 | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | $0.0069 |
| deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash | 3 | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | $0.0000 |
| google/gemini-3.1-pro-preview | 0 | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | $0.0000 |

GPT and DeepSeek fully worked through the proxy — tools, streaming, resume, all real. Gemini failed before any tool call on a schema incompatibility (flagged for the mastermind, not something I fixed).

**Provider wiring**: any `spawn_agent` call with a `model` containing `/` now runs through OpenRouter automatically — no code elsewhere has to change. Real cost comes from OpenRouter's own numbers, not the SDK's wrong guess. `review.mjs --model <slug>` already works via the same rule.

Committed as `b7fd00d9` (spike) and `556dea2e` (wiring) in worktree `qf-7`. Full detail is in the task log; the parent mastermind owns merging.

All my fence's changes are committed cleanly (3rd commit `53852db6`). The remaining modified/untracked `files.jsonl` entries across the whole repo are pre-existing, out-of-fence auto-generated index files unrelated to my task — not mine to touch or commit.

**Status: confirmed complete, nothing lost in the restart.** My last tool call (the report to `task-mastermind-openrouter`) had already completed and returned successfully before the restart — nothing was left hanging. Three commits in worktree `qf-7`:

- `b7fd00d9` — spike.mjs + provider.js + real results (spike.jsonl)
- `556dea2e` — provider field wired into every spawn (Agents.js, tiers.js, tools.js, review.mjs, readme.md)
- `53852db6` — picked up a late `spike.jsonl` row (someone else tried `google/gemini-3.8-flash` after my report — same tool-schema 400, so the Gemini issue isn't specific to one model) and the Servex-restart marker

All five deliverables are done, tested (`provider.test.mjs` 6/6 passing with no key), and reported to the parent mastermind with the spike table. Nothing further to do on this brief — the parent task owns merging.

Both follow-ups are done, verified, committed, and reported:

**1. Gemini 400 — found and fixed:** the offending tool was the built-in `ArtifactData` (not one of ours) — its `query.where` param is an array of `[field, op, value]` tuples that declares `prefixItems` but no `items` on the inner array, which Gemini's strict validator rejects before any tool call. Dropped it for `google/*` models via a new `disallowed_tools_for(model)` in `provider.js`, wired into both `spike.mjs` and `Agents.js`. Reran the spike on both Gemini models — the 400 is gone:

| model | tools | stream | edit | resume ok | $real |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| google/gemini-3.1-pro-preview | 0 | true | false | true | $0.0108 |
| google/gemini-3.8-flash | 3 | true | true | true | $0.0714 |

`gemini-3.8-flash` fully passed; `gemini-3.1-pro-preview` hit one separate transient stream error (not the schema bug) — flagged to the mastermind rather than chased further.

**2. Cost bug — fixed:** `refresh_or_cost()` was overwriting `this.cost` with each turn's delta instead of accumulating; now keeps a running `or_cost`. `result()`/`compact_done()` no longer let `total_cost_usd` touch cost for an openrouter agent. Documented the shared-key mis-attribution caveat as asked.

Committed in `f67d73af` (code) and `c923ec59` (log), test suite 7/7, and the full table reported back to `task-mastermind-openrouter`.

Phase 2 item 1 (the spend guard) is done and reported. Summary:

- **Cap**: `Agents.spawn()` refuses an OpenRouter spawn (one clear line) once today's spend hits `SERVEX_OR_DAILY_CAP` (default $8) or credit drops under $1 — checked via a lazily-started 30s cache so it never adds a network call to the hot path or to unrelated test imports, and fails closed if it can't read the key.
- **Ledger**: every settled turn appends one line to the `openrouter` log through Servex's single-writer `Log`, no second writer.
- **Dashboard**: one more bar in the existing `usage_rail()` meter (same component the Claude 5h/weekly windows use), with credit-left in the label — no new widget.

Commits `836d93f5` (code) and `bab5a0bb` (log), `provider.test.mjs` at 12/12. Left `Servex/ext/openrouter/evals/` untouched for the other minion, and flagged (with a verified false-positive note) a health-check hook that fired twice on an unrelated, pre-existing `usage.json` 404. Reported the full table and detail to `task-mastermind-openrouter`; standing by for the next ask.

Done for this phase. Summary:

**Built** `Servex/ext/openrouter/evals/rules.mjs` — five known-answer tests (CLAUDE.md, readme chain, tool calls, the `append.mjs` house convention, and staying inside a fence under a tempting bait), each spawning one real Servex agent and checked by script, never judgment.

**Proved it works**: all 5 pass for real against `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001`, ~$0.56 total, committed as `1d5219a0`.

**Changed course mid-task**: the parent mastermind asked me to share results with mastermind-servex-9's probe system instead of building a second format — done, both now write `{"probe":{...}}` lines to `Servex/ext/openrouter/evals/results.jsonl`, via the validated `append.mjs` hook.

**Reported** the Haiku table and two open items (a stale test-bug FAIL line in the shared results file, and that my brief's task dir existed only in the main tree, not the worktree I was told to work in) to the parent, and I'm now waiting on it before spending on any real OpenRouter model, per the brief.
Reported both fixes to `task-mastermind-openrouter`, ready for merge. Standing by for its response.
